Article Title: 'We don't want a fight': Delhi traders' body writes to Rahul Gandhi again over November 1 rally
Article Text:
Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi (File photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A Delhi traders' body on Wednesday wrote another letter to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , urging him to postpone the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan until after Diwali over fears that the gathering could disrupt business in several major markets.The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI), which has raised concerns about the rally's impact on festive sales, also sought a 20-minute meeting with Gandhi to explain why traders want the event deferred.In the letter, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said representatives of 20 markets wanted an opportunity to put forward their concerns about the rally, which is expected to draw around 10 lakh people."We don't want a fight; we want dialogue. Rahul ji himself says that he listens to everyone, listens to the voice of small traders. So, we traders from 20 markets are asking him for 20 minutes. This will be the beauty of democracy," Goyal said.The traders' body also proposed that it would withdraw its protest if Gandhi could convince its representatives that the rally would bring more customers and boost business. However, if traders were able to convince him that the event would result in losses, they wanted him to agree to postpone it until after Diwali.Wednesday's letter was the second sent by CTI to Gandhi within four days. The organisation had first approached the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha on October 24, seeking postponement of the rally to prevent disruptions during one of the busiest periods for Delhi's markets.According to CTI, at least 20 markets within a 1-5 km radius of Ramlila Maidan could be affected by the expected turnout.The markets include Chandni Chowk, Bhagirath Palace, Khari Baoli, Sadar Bazar, Chawri Bazar, Kashmere Gate, Nabi Karim, Karol Bagh, Ajmeri Gate and Daryaganj.Nai Sarak, Kinari Bazar, Dariba Kalan, Fatehpuri, Naya Bazar, Filmistan, Paharganj, Gaffar Market, Jama Masjid-Meena Bazar and Lajpat Rai Market are also among the commercial areas identified by the traders' body.The concerns come as the INDIA bloc prepares for a major show of strength in the national capital over alleged "vote chori" and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The opposition alliance has called the November 1 rally to step up pressure on the government and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The rally follows a series of demonstrations by opposition parties over the electoral-roll revision exercise.On October 12, opposition leaders, including Gandhi, joined activists and civil society members in a 'March for Democracy' along a heavily barricaded route near the Supreme Court in Delhi. A joint petition challenging the SIR was also filed.A day later, Gandhi hosted INDIA bloc leaders for tea at his residence. Following the meeting, the opposition alliance vowed to continue its campaign and take the fight to its logical conclusion.
Article Summary: The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has raised concerns about the rally's impact on festive sales. It also sought a 20-minute meeting with Gandhi to explain why traders want the event deferred. The concerns come as the INDIA bloc prepares for a major show of strength in the national capital over alleged "vote chori"

Article Title: Delhi to Haridwar in 90 minutes? What Nitin Gadkari said
Article Text:
Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari announced a new road project connecting Delhi to Haridwar. (Pic Credit: PTI)

Expressways to open up new economic opportunities

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

100 invested in infrastructure can create 325 economic impact: Gadkari

The journey from Delhi to Haridwar may soon become significantly shorter, with a new road project scheduled to open next month, union road hransport and Highways minister Nitin Gadkari said on Tuesday. Once operational, the route could bring travel time down to around 90 minutes.Speaking at the Confederation of Indian Industry’s (CII) National Conference on ‘Highways of India’s Future: Smart, Safe and Sustainable’, Gadkari said the expansion of the country’s road network was making religious destinations more accessible while supporting tourism and job creation.Pointing to the recently opened Delhi-Dehradun corridor, the minister said the journey between the two cities, which earlier took about seven hours, could now be completed in roughly two hours.He said the upcoming Delhi-Haridwar project would further improve access to one of the country’s prominent pilgrimage destinations, according to ET.Gadkari also cited road development work in Ayodhya and Maharashtra, including the Pandharpur Palkhi Marg projects, which are intended to make journeys easier for devotees. He said infrastructure development was being undertaken across regions, with roads, tunnels and bridges being built in the Northeast, Jammu and Kashmir and other parts of the country.Gadkari said greenfield expressways could bring regions with limited economic opportunities closer to major business centres, helping expand development beyond established urban hubs.The Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, he said, would improve access for rural areas, aspirational districts and tribal regions. In Haryana, the project is expected to benefit aspirational districts, while Alwar, Dausa, Sawai Madhopur and Bundi in Rajasthan are among the areas that could gain from improved road links.He also pointed to Ratlam and Jhabua in Madhya Pradesh and Dahod in Gujarat, highlighting the potential for better connectivity to encourage economic activity in tribal districts.Stressing the importance of the Delhi-Mumbai route, Gadkari said stronger links between the national capital and Mumbai were crucial, given the latter’s position as the country’s economic hub.The minister said infrastructure spending has benefits beyond the construction of roads, as projects generate employment and increase demand for cement, steel and construction equipment.He added that improved connectivity could lower transportation costs and make the movement of goods and people more efficient. These gains, he said, could benefit businesses, tourism and the development of towns.Describing infrastructure as a key driver of economic growth, Gadkari said every 100 invested in the sector could produce an economic impact of 325.“If we spend 100 on infrastructure, the impact on the economy comes to 325. GDP is also going to increase,” he said.Gadkari added that the government was continuing to focus on expressways and greenfield highways to improve links between regions, strengthen economic activity and support development across India.
Article Summary: Road transport and Highways minister Nitin Gadkari announced a new road project connecting Delhi to Haridwar. Once operational, the route could bring travel time down to around 90 minutes. He said the expansion of the country’s road network was making religious destinations more accessible while supporting tourism.

Article Title: India invites Pakistan for SCO civilisational dialogue forum meet next month
Article Text:
File photo: India and Pakistan flags (Image enhanced using AI)

NEW DELHI: India has invited Pakistan for the inaugural meeting of the SCO civilisational dialogue forum that it will host next month.Prime Minister Narendra Modi had proposed the dialogue forum during his visit to Tianjin last year for the SCO summit, saying that it would work to foster greater people-to-people ties and cultural understanding within the grouping.Aurungzeb Khan Khichi, minister for national heritage and culture, has been invited for the dialogue.The Eurasian bloc continues to enjoy immunity from India-Pakistan tensions, allowing rare high-level visits from both sides even in the absence of any substantive bilateral engagement between the two countries for over a decade.The last Pakistan minister to visit India was Bilawal Bhutto in 2023 for a meeting of the SCO foreign ministers.External affairs minister S Jaishankar travelled to Pakistan the next year for the meeting of SCO heads of govt. On both occasions, there was no bilateral meeting.The invitation for the civilisational dialogue comes weeks after India sent its SCO national coordinator Alok Dimri to Pakistan for a high-level meeting to finalise the grouping’s agenda and meetings in the run-up to the Islamabad summit next year.Pakistan currently holds the SCO presidency and will host the heads of state summit next year. SCO national coordinator Dimri’s visit was the first senior-level visit from either side since the Pahalgam terror attack.
Article Summary: India has invited Pakistan for the inaugural meeting of the SCO civilisational dialogue forum that it will host next month. Prime Minister Narendra Modi had proposed the dialogue forum during his visit to Tianjin last year. The Eurasian bloc continues to enjoy immunity from India-Pakistan tensions.

Article Title: SC: Cannot let pharma industry ‘run amok’ in name of free market
Article Text:
SC questioned the Centre over pharma companies pricing medicines at over 1,000% of cost, saying the industry can't "run amok" in the name of free market.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday said the pharma industry cannot be allowed to “run amok” in the name of free market to fix the maximum retail price (MRP) of medicines at an exponentially high level, which in some cases happens to be over 1,000% of the price at which they are sold to retailers.Expressing anguish over the suffering of the common man who had to pay the price, a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said the court is “pained by the loot” and repeatedly asked Centre to explain the rationale behind allowing a high MRP and who ultimately benefits from the policy. It reserved its order on plea to bring all non-patented medicines and medical consumables under price control mechanism like scheduled drugs.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, who had to face a volley of questions from the bench, tried to convince the court that govt was aware of the problem and that was why it recently decided to cap the price of anti-cancer drugs. But the court responded that govt “woke up” only after it intervened and passed harsh observations on the prevailing system.She, however, said the deliberation was already on and SC’s intervention expedited it.“People are living in a daydream that someday they will benefit from the drugs prices control order (DPCO)... The policy is only to give benefit to the corporate. We are thinking from the point of view of poor patients,” SC observed. Bhati, thereafter, submitted that medicine prices in India are among the lowest in the world due to free market and govt cannot take control of the entire pharma market, but the bench told her, “You are either not aware about the problem or not keen to solve the problem... Why is the entire system working for the benefit of few people?”“Ordinarily, where there is substantial competition, there is no need to regulate prices. It is not that the govt has left the market unregulated but the complete control of the market is not feasible,” Bhati said, adding that the issue pertains to economic policy and commerce and the court should desist from interfering. Not convinced by this, the bench said, “Should they (pharma companies) be allowed to run amok? What is the justification for the difference in prices? You are not able to come with an answer. We have asked you 30 times. Do not talk about control... You are talking about economic policy and commerce. Is commerce more important than the life of citizens and be given precedence?”
Article Summary: Supreme Court said the pharma industry cannot be allowed to “run amok’ in the name of free market. Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta repeatedly asked Centre to explain the rationale behind allowing a high MRP. It reserved its order on plea to bring all non-patented medicines and medical consumables under price control mechanism.

Article Title: A decade after liquor ban, Bihar faces a new drug question: What the numbers reveal
Article Text:
NCB destroyed 1,170.15 kg of seized narcotics worth Rs 4.54 crore in Patna, Bihar, across four cases to prevent their recirculation in September (Credit: NCB's X)

Does Bihar have a new drug problem?

Where are the drugs coming from?

Cops suggest that drugs in Bihar enters from multiple states

Is the trade limited to transportation?

Is Bihar seeing a rise in consumption or a rise in detection?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Does Bihar have a new drug problem?

Punjab is set to go to polls in 2027, and the BJP, seeking to form its first government in the state, has made the drug menace a major election issue. The party has been targeting the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) over its handling of the problem. Union home minister Amit Shah has even promised to make Punjab "drug-free" by December 2029 if the BJP comes to power.But AAP has hit back. Its national convener Arvind Kejriwal questioned the BJP over the drug problem in states where it is in power, including Bihar, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Goa, asking why the same deadline had not been set for them.The political exchange has also put the focus on Bihar, where alcohol has been banned for a decade but recent drug seizures have raised fresh concerns. More than 4.13 lakh intoxicating injections were seized in Patna in the first eight months of 2026, while investigations have uncovered heroin consignments, codeine-based cough syrup and networks involved in preparing and distributing narcotics.But what do these seizures actually reveal? Is Bihar witnessing a rise in drug consumption, or is the state increasingly becoming a transit route for narcotics headed elsewhere? And has a decade of prohibition had any bearing on the availability and use of other intoxicants? Here's what the data revealsMore than 4.13 lakh intoxicating injections seized in Patna in the first eight months of 2026.A sharp rise in smack seizures. Growing quantities of codeine-based cough syrup being intercepted. Across Bihar, recent drug seizures and investigations point to a changing narcotics landscape, raising questions about what is entering the state, where it is going and who is using it.But do these seizures signal a growing drug problem within Bihar, or are they exposing the scale of a trafficking network that uses the state as a transit route? Police have traced consignments from the Northeast and Nepal-linked routes, while investigations in Patna have uncovered alleged local networks involved in preparing and distributing narcotics.The answers are not straightforward. Five years of seizure data show sharp fluctuations rather than a consistent rise across substances. Meanwhile, a debate over Bihar’s liquor prohibition has raised another question about whether the use of alternative intoxicants has changed since the ban came into force in 2016.What do the numbers reveal?Bihar’s drug seizure data over five years shows that ganja accounted for the largest quantities seized among the major narcotics listed, while seizures of heroin fluctuated sharply. Ganja seizures rose from 16,607 kg in 2020 to 33,603 kg in 2021, before falling to 23,023 kg in 2022 and 13,129 kg in 2023. They increased again to 18,356 kg in 2024.Heroin seizures fell from 363.77 kg in 2020 to 9.62 kg in 2021, before rising to 31.13 kg in 2022, 27.37 kg in 2023 and 53.35 kg in 2024. Hashish seizures also varied, peaking at 395.12 kg in 2021 before declining to 195 kg in 2024.A person whose circle consumes drugs said, on the condition of anonymity, that marijuana remained the most widely consumed substance in their social circle and that they had not noticed a significant shift in preferences towards other drugs.“In most circles, marijuana is most widely consumed, and I don't think synthetic drugs have made their way to Bihar,” the person said.The data records smaller seizures of other substances, including ATS, cocaine and LSD in certain years. While these figures show fluctuations in the quantities of narcotics seized, they do not establish a steady year-on-year rise in drug trafficking or consumption. Seizure figures reflect what enforcement agencies intercept and, on their own, cannot establish how many people use drugs or whether drug abuse is increasing in Bihar.Police say a significant share of narcotics reaching Patna comes from the Northeast. The routes and methods of transportation vary according to the size of a consignment.Investigations have also pointed to supply chains passing through multiple states. In September, four people were arrested near JP Setu in Patna with 274 gm of heroin. Police traced the consignment to Assam, from where it allegedly travelled to Tamkuhi in Kushinagar, Uttar Pradesh, before being sent towards Patna.Bihar’s location along the Nepal border adds another dimension to the problem. On October 25, Motihari Police, in a joint operation with the Bihar Special Task Force, seized smack valued at Rs 4 crore near Raxaul, close to the India-Nepal border.In a separate operation, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence’s Muzaffarpur unit and the Bihar STF busted a suspected network involved in smuggling Nepal-origin charas into India. Two people were arrested and 5.14 kg of charas, valued by officials at Rs 5.14 crore, was seized. Investigators said the consignment was intended for onward transportation to Indore in Madhya Pradesh.The cases point to Bihar’s role as a route for narcotics moving between regions. However, seizures along transport corridors do not establish how much of the intercepted supply is consumed within the state.Police investigations suggest that local networks are also involved in storage, preparation and distribution.In March, police found a rented room in Patna’s Ramakrishna Nagar area allegedly being used to prepare smack. A flat in Alamganj was allegedly used for distribution. Police recovered 1.68 kg of brown sugar and cash, along with cheques worth around Rs 70 lakh issued in the name of a police officer.The trade is not confined to substances traditionally associated with narcotics smuggling. Pharmaceutical products have also featured in investigations. In May, the DRI seized 7,500 bottles of codeine-based cough syrup from a pickup van outside Patna’s Rajendra Nagar Terminal. Investigators found that the consignee’s drug licence had been cancelled and that the firm did not exist at its stated address.Such cases raise questions about how pharmaceutical products enter illicit supply chains, how they are distributed and whether existing monitoring systems are able to detect diversion from legitimate channels.A Patna high court order has raised questions about how narcotics can travel long distances before being intercepted.In an order dated September 15, the court expressed concern over two minor boys who had travelled from Assam to Bihar in a car without a registration certificate. The vehicle was intercepted near Patna, and the directorate of revenue intelligence recovered more than 60 kg of cannabis from a concealed compartment.The court questioned how the vehicle had travelled uninterrupted from Assam to Bihar while carrying a commercial quantity of cannabis.Has prohibition changed pattern of substance use?Bihar banned the sale and consumption of alcohol in April 2016 under a policy introduced by the Nitish Kumar government. The prohibition was intended, among other objectives, to reduce domestic violence and encourage households to spend money on more productive needs.A research paper by the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER), titled Macro Perspective of Bihar's Development Achievements, Unfinished Agenda, and the Way Forward, has questioned whether the ban achieved its intended outcomes.The paper said reported crimes against women had not declined following prohibition and that total reported crimes against women increased over the post-2016 period. It also pointed to concerns about the expansion of illicit liquor trade, enforcement challenges, corruption and the use of alternative intoxicants, including illicit drugs."In tandem, there was a significant rise in illegal liquor trade leading to higher alcohol consumption, increased crime and corruption, and an increase in the use of alternative additive substances, such as illicit drugs," the paper said.The authors argued that Bihar should reconsider prohibition and restore alcohol excise duty to historical levels. They estimated that doing so could increase the state’s own revenues by 14-15%.Some residents also believe prohibition may be one factor behind the availability of other intoxicants, although personal accounts cannot establish a direct link between the ban and drug consumption.“I would argue that it is a byproduct of the prohibition in the state, but that isn't the full picture,” another person who spoke on condition of anonymity said, referring to the perceived increase in drug availability.The person said their observations were based on the experiences of people in their social circle who use drugs, adding that young people and those in their 30s appeared to be among the users they had noticed.“In a state like Bihar, with a large chunk of youth population that haven't so far been backed with job opportunities, [this] has also contributed to the rise of drug consumption in the state,” the person said.They also flagged a lack of awareness about addiction and the support available to people who use drugs.“I feel like there is a lack of awareness against remedial methods, like what to do if someone you know has become addicted to drugs, what are you supposed to do then. I feel like there is a lack of rehabilitation system and awareness among the people needed to curb the drug menace,” the person said.The distinction matters because seizures measure what enforcement agencies intercept, not the total volume of drugs entering the market or being consumed.Bihar’s prohibition and narcotics enforcement policies also form part of a wider debate over how the state measures the effectiveness of its policing. A rise in seizures can reflect an increase in trafficking, improved detection or a combination of both.Bihar minister Madan Sahni has rejected the charge that rising seizures indicate a failure of prohibition. He said the increase was not confined to Bihar but was a phenomenon seen in other states as well."I must say that due to the alertness of the officials concerned, the quantity of the seizure of substances prohibited under the NDPS Act has increased in the state, but at the same time, people should know that the majority of the prohibited substances seized in Bihar are meant for supply to other states," he said.Sahni added that intercepting consignments within Bihar could create the impression that the drugs were intended for local consumption, even when they were being transported elsewhere. He also defended prohibition, saying it had been successful.The minister’s argument points to an important gap in the available figures. Without comparable data on drug use, treatment demand, drug-related health emergencies and the destinations of intercepted consignments, it is difficult to determine how much of the rise reflects local consumption.RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha, meanwhile, cited a media report and said the situation was out of control."An entire generation has been ruined. This is what happens when the government has no control. The situation here is completely out of control..." he said.Bihar’s recent seizure figures and investigations point to a changing narcotics landscape. Police have reported sharp increases in some categories, identified supply routes running through several states and uncovered alleged local networks involved in preparation and distribution. Seizures near the Nepal border have also highlighted the state’s role in cross-border trafficking.But the central question remains unresolved. Is Bihar facing a growing drug-consumption problem, a trafficking problem that extends beyond its borders, or both?
Article Summary: NCB destroyed 1,170.15 kg of seized narcotics worth Rs 4.54 crore in Patna, Bihar, across four cases to prevent their recirculation in September. More than 4.13 lakh intoxicating injections were seized in the first eight months of 2026, while investigations have uncovered heroin consignments, codeine-based cough syrup and networks involved in preparing and distributing narcotics.

Article Title: Aviation ministry suspends operations at three Andhra airports as Cyclone Arnab intensifies
Article Text:
File photo: Two people holding an umbrella brave strong winds and rain as high tide waves hit the coast ahead of the impending landfall of cyclonic storm 'Arnab', in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh.

Flight operations suspended at three Andhra airports

NEW DELHI: The ministry of civil aviation on Tuesday reviewed aviation safety and operational readiness as Cyclone Arnab is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and cross the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28, bringing winds of 125–135 kmph and gusts of up to 150 kmph, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).In a statement issued by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the ministry said flights to and from coastal Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha, including Bhubaneswar, were expected to be among the most affected. Hyderabad, Varanasi, Prayagraj and Gorakhpur could also see knock-on delays depending on the storm’s track.The ministry reviewed preparedness with the Airports Authority of India (AAI), Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS), IMD, airlines, airport operators, the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and disaster management authorities in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal, among other agencies.According to the ministry, operations at Visakhapatnam airport were suspended from the afternoon of October 27. Flights at Vijayawada and Rajahmundry airports were suspended after 7pm the same day. The Delhi–Bhogapuram–Delhi service has also been cancelled for October 28.Airlines have announced cancellations and operational changes:Six cancellations on the Delhi–Visakhapatnam–Delhi route on October 27 and the Delhi–Vijayawada–Delhi route on October 28.Thirteen cancellations, mainly affecting Visakhapatnam services to and from Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Vijayawada. Varanasi–Bangkok and Bangkok–Visakhapatnam flights have also been cancelled.All flights at Visakhapatnam have been suspended, along with services at Vijayawada and Rajahmundry after 7pm on October 27. The ministry said cancellation figures were provisional.Delhi–Bhogapuram and return flights scheduled for October 28 have been cancelled. All other flights were expected to operate.Operations were continuing normally, with no cancellations reported so far.The ministry has advised airlines to follow operational guidelines for adverse weather, inform passengers about delays and cancellations, and comply with applicable rebooking and refund rules.Passengers have been urged to check their flight status through their airline’s website, app, helpline or SMS before leaving for the airport, and not to travel unless their flight is confirmed. They have also been advised to allow extra time for their journeys, as waterlogging and road closures are likely in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.The ministry said the aviation secretary had asked airlines and airport operators to provide additional assistance to senior citizens, persons with reduced mobility, parents travelling with infants and passengers requiring medical support.Passengers with unresolved complaints have been advised to approach the airline first and then escalate the matter through the AirSewa portal or app.The ministry said passenger safety remained its top priority and that further updates would be issued as weather conditions changed.
Article Summary: Cyclone Arnab is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm. Flights to and from coastal Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha are expected to be among the most affected. Hyderabad, Varanasi, Prayagraj and Gorakhpur could also see knock-on delays.

Article Title: Poll panel keeps RTI applicant waiting for reply
Article Text:
File photo: Election Commision of India

EC is yet to respond to an RTI application seeking details of steps taken to address grievances raised by two ECs and copies of files, including notings, related to the issue, despite the 30-day statutory time-limit for giving a reply lapsing, said applicant Commodore Lokesh K Batra (retd) Tuesday. The application was filed on Sept 25 but the RTI status on EC’s website shows “32 day” and still “in-progress”, Batra said, asking “why EC is maintaining a deafening silence” and “what is EC hiding?” The activist sought copies of the complete set of records of issues and grievances raised by ECs SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.On Sept 24, in a separate RTI to cabinet secretariat, Batra sought copies of the EC’s communications, details of steps taken and file notings. He received a response on Oct 19, and documents and file notings on Oct 22.
Article Summary: EC is yet to respond to an RTI application seeking details of steps taken to address grievances raised by two ECs. The 30-day statutory time-limit for giving a reply lapsing. The application was filed on Sept 25 but the RTI status on EC’s website shows ‘32 day’

Article Title: Ladakh government reaches out to protesters demanding liquor ban
Article Text:
File photo: Ladakh's Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Amid protests by women in large numbers demanding a ban on liquor and declaring Ladakh a dry Union Territory, the administration on Tuesday asked the Ladakhi Buddhist Association’s women’s wing to have wider consultations to build consensus on the issue and find a middle ground.The protesters are affiliated with various religious and social organisations, including the Ladakh Buddhist Association (LBA), Anjuman Imamia, Anjuman Moin-ul-Islam and the Christian community.A Ladakh govt spokesperson said chief secretary Ashish Kundra held a meeting with women representatives of various religious organisations on Tuesday, which was also attended by representatives of tourism bodies.According to the spokesman, the participants were informed that the number of retail liquor vends was two till last year and only is functional this year. “Similarly, the number of functional bars attached to restaurants offering retail sale of liquor, which was earlier 23, had increased by 17 newly issued licences, taking the total to 40.”While the chief secretary acknowledged the concerns expressed by the women representatives, he also said that the demand for declaring Ladakh a completely dry UT is a significant matter that requires careful deliberation and consultation with all stakeholders, for which all agreed to.Kundra cited the experience of other states like Bihar and Haryana where complete prohibition had led to serious consequences of spurious liquor and drugs being proliferated. “There are also issues of employment, tourism and economic activity. Consultation with the hotel industry is also crucial, particularly when tourism is the primary economic activity in the territory,” the spokesperson said, quoting the chief secretary.
Article Summary: The protesters are affiliated with various religious and social organisations. Chief secretary Ashish Kundra held a meeting with women representatives of various religious organisations. The meeting was also attended by representatives of tourism bodies. Kundra cited the experience of other states like Bihar and Haryana where complete prohibition had led to serious consequences.

Article Title: Build AI to secure systems, serve humanity: PM Modi
Article Text:
File photo: Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the inauguration of the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026, in New Delhi.

NEW DELHI: AI can give us answers quickly, but testing their veracity must remain the scientist’s responsibility, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said Tuesday, urging scientists to innovate boldly.Speaking at ‘Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave’, Modi referred to AI-era cybersecurity threats to financial networks and national security, calling for AI-based and quantum security solutions to protect national systems and serve humanity. “In the age of AI, there are challenges. While AI can execute tasks to boost productivity, it must enrich rather than restrict independent thinking, allowing researchers to use saved time for harder problems, new experiments and idea validation,” he said.The PM’s remarks came amid calls for AI regulation over fears it may go rogue, as the govt drafts a consultation paper on India’s AI policy.Modi said a ‘Viksit Bharat’ (developed India) would rest on scientific research, discoveries and innovation. He urged researchers, industry leaders, startup founders and students to set a three-year target for developing a technology, prototype, pilot project or product that could make India a global hub for solutions.Modi said India must prepare a generation that leads emerging science and technology, not merely participates in it, and called for expanding the country’s strength in critical technologies.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke at ‘Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave’ Modi referred to AI-era cybersecurity threats to financial networks and national security. PM’s remarks came amid calls for AI regulation over fears it may go rogue.

Article Title: Who named Cyclone Arnab and why? Where it will hit, states on alert and preparedness
Article Text:
Rough sea conditions prevail ahead of the expected landfall, in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh

Why is it named Arnab? How storm naming works

Andhra Pradesh braces for landfall

Odisha, Jharkhand face heavy rain, strong winds

West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh also likely to see unseasonal rain

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India is bracing for Cyclone Arnab as it moves towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, with landfall expected by Wednesday forenoon as authorities expect strong winds, heavy rainfall and possible flooding across several states. Cyclone Arnab is drawing attention not only for its projected impact along the Andhra Pradesh coast but also for its name.Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast maximum sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, with gusts reaching 140 kmph, when the storm crosses the coast near Yanam, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. Its effects are expected in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh, prompting weather alerts and precautionary measures.The name Arnab was contributed by Bangladesh to the list of names used for tropical cyclones over the North Indian Ocean. It is pronounced “Ornab”.Cyclone names in the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea are assigned by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO)/United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) Panel on Tropical Cyclones. The naming system began in 2004, with the list subsequently expanded as more countries joined the panel.The current list contains 52 names contributed by 13 countries: Bangladesh, India, Iran, Maldives, Myanmar, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Thailand, the United Arab Emirates and Yemen. The list was adopted in April 2020.Names are used sequentially, column-wise, according to the established list. Each name is used only once and is not repeated in subsequent lists. The Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre in New Delhi, operated by the IMD, is responsible for naming cyclones that form over the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea once they reach the prescribed intensity.Naming storms helps meteorological agencies, governments, disaster management authorities and the public identify and communicate warnings about individual weather systems more easily.The cyclone was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal on Tuesday morning, moving west-northwestwards before its expected turn towards the coast. The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) has warned of heavy rainfall in northern coastal districts, including Srikakulam, with strong winds already affecting parts of the coast.Authorities have identified 16 districts, covering 2,460 revenue villages and 92 urban areas, as potentially vulnerable. According to the state disaster management authorities, 1,763 cyclone shelters have been readied, 2,907 control rooms established and 3,185 nodal officers deployed. National and state disaster response teams have also been positioned in 11 high-risk districts.Authorities have banned public access to beaches and announced restrictions on coastal road movement. Fishing vessels have been secured at harbours, with the APSDMA saying 30,043 fishing vessels have been anchored.Air India has warned that adverse weather could affect flights to and from Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada on October 27. Passengers have been advised to check their flight status and allow additional time for travel to airports. Ashwini Vaishnaw said safety protocols and rapid restoration measures were in place across the Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam divisions ahead of Cyclone Arnab’s expected landfall on October 28. In a post on X, he said war rooms were active at zonal, divisional and Railway Board levels, with around 600 km of track under close watch. “Passenger safety is the top priority,” Vaishnaw said, adding that relief wagons, diesel locomotives, ambulances and restoration equipment had been stationed at key locations, while wind speeds and water levels were being monitored hourly. He also said coordination with the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and state disaster authorities was under way.Odisha has already experienced heavy rain and strong winds in parts of the state. The IMD has issued an orange warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall, ranging from 12 cm to 20 cm, in Puri, Gajapati, Ganjam, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri. A yellow warning has been issued for several other districts.Tourist boat and ferry operations at Chilika Lake have been suspended from October 26 to 29 as a precaution. Authorities have moved boats to safer locations, while Paradip Port has provided shelter to 305 fishermen at its Eastern Quay-1 berth.In Jharkhand, the state government has directed district administrations to remain vigilant. A yellow alert for heavy rain has been issued for several districts on October 28, followed by orange alerts for parts of the state through October 30. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds are also expected.The Ranchi district administration has warned of waterlogging, overflowing drains and water bodies, damage to weak structures and possible flood-like conditions in low-lying areas. Standing crops could also be affected by water accumulation.The cyclone's influence is expected to extend to West Bengal between October 28 and 30. In south Bengal, heavy rainfall is forecast in South 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, Paschim Medinipur, Jhargram, Purulia, Bankura and Paschim Bardhaman on October 28 and 29. Kolkata is likely to receive light to moderate rain over the next 48 hours.In the sub-Himalayan region, Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Alipurduar and Jalpaiguri are likely to experience heavy rain on October 29 and 30. The IMD has also advised fishermen not to venture into the sea until October 29, warning of rough to very rough conditions and squally winds of 40-50 kmph, gusting up to 60 kmph, along and off the West Bengal coast.Uttar Pradesh is forecast to receive unseasonal rain, thunderstorms and strong winds between October 28 and 31. The IMD has issued alerts for several districts, with heavy rain possible in parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh, Awadh and the Terai region. Daytime temperatures could fall by 5-8 degrees Celsius in some areas on October 30.Authorities have advised residents to follow official weather bulletins, avoid unnecessary travel during storms and stay away from trees, electricity poles, weak structures and open fields during lightning.
Article Summary: The name Arnab was contributed by Bangladesh to the list of names used for tropical cyclones over the North Indian Ocean. The cyclone was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal on Tuesday morning, moving west-northwestwards before its expected turn towards the coast. Authorities have identified 16 districts, covering 2,460 revenue villages and 92 urban areas as potentially vulnerable.

Article Title: Need to balance right to free speech, privacy: Supreme Court
Article Text:
Right to free speech of media needs balancing with privacy of citizens: SC

Privacy act will hit freedom of Press: Digital news body

NEW DELHI: SC on Tuesday acknowledged the importance of media’s right to freedom of speech and expression but said this needed to be balanced with citizens’ right to privacy and dignity and asked petitioner Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) to suggest how these two rights could coexist harmoniously.Entertaining DNPA’s petition terming certain provisions of Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and the amendment to RTI Act redefining ‘personal information’ as an attempt towards pre-censorship of news content that violated the media’s right to free speech and impeded media independence, SC said, “You are domain experts. You suggest to the govt and SC how to harmonise the two competing rights.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymlaya Bagchi and V Mohana said: “Media must ensure there is no misuse of the rights enjoyed by it. There must be a balance between your rights and the rights of innocent citizens. We will have to leave it to you to suggest how best you are going to ensure that the media’s rights are not misused and the right to privacy of citizens are not violated.”Appearing for the petitioner, senior advocate Madhavi Divan said provisions of DPDP Act failed to provide exemption in favour of journalistic activity as a distinct class and had brought the regime of notice and prior consent within it, which would lead to closure of newsrooms as they feed live information.If journalists went around seeking consent of people, then no news could be disseminated, she said.“It is not merely the fundamental right to speech and expression and dissemination of information owing to freedom of the press which has been set at nought by the aforesaid provision, but the DPDP Act places myriad restrictions in the manner in which information is accessed, processed and disseminated,” DNPA said.“In the absence of exemptions, the entire scheme under Chapter II of DPDP Act will constitute unreasonable restrictions upon journalists in the exercise of the fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression and practise any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade or business,” it added.The petitioner complained that DPDP Act imposed onerous conditions governing how information was to be disseminated and how access was obtained and cited an SC judgement, which had ruled that the fundamental right to know could not be sacrificed at the altar of privacy.The bench issued notice to the Centre on the petition and tagged it with a clutch of petitions which are scheduled for hearing on Nov 17.
Article Summary: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and amendment to RTI Act redefining ‘personal information’ were cited as an attempt towards pre-censorship of news content. SC asked petitioner Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) to suggest how these two rights could coexist harmoniously.

NEW DELHI: General medicine accounted for more allotments than radiodiagnosis among top entries in the first round of NEET-PG 2026 counselling, highlighting the competing career attractions of the two sought-after PG specialties, reports Anuja Jaiswal.An analysis of Medical Counselling Committee’s Round 1 allotment list shows 51 allotments in general medicine as against 28 in radiodiagnosis among the first 100 entries. Dermatology was a distant third with six allotments, while paediatrics and general surgery had three each. Doctors say the choices reflect different career priorities. General medicine, on the other hand, remains an evergreen specialty, offering opportunities to pursue super-specialisation and earn more in the long run. However, financial settlement can take longer, as candidates must complete a DM course and then build their practice, which could take another two to three years.“General medicine appeals to candidates who enjoy clinical challenges, patient interaction and managing complex diseases.While the financial rewards may take longer to materialise, the scope for super-specialisation and professional growth is immense. Ultimately, the choice should be guided by what fulfils you as a doctor, not just by how quickly you can start earning,” said Prof Neeraj Nischal, internal medicine, AIIMS.According to a senior doctor, radiology is attractive because it offers good earning potential early in one’s career. However, with AI advancing rapidly, some candidates may also be weighing the technology’s long-term impact on the specialty.While this does not mean that human expertise will not be needed, the growing role of AI could influence how students assess radiology as a career choice.
Article Summary: General medicine accounted for more allotments than radiodiagnosis among top entries in the first round of NEET-PG 2026 counselling. General medicine remains an evergreen specialty, offering opportunities to pursue super-specialisation.

NEW DELHI: India must embrace the future technologies, innovate boldly and lead the world in developing them, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said while addressing the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave here on Tuesday.Asserting that a ‘Viksit Bharat’ (developed India) will be built on strong foundations of scientific research, discoveries and the spirit of innovation, he appealed to every researcher, industry leader, startup founder and student to set a concrete three-year target identifying which technology, prototype, pilot project or product they will help develop to make India a global hub for solutions.Underlining how scientific judgement will evolve in the age of AI during the second quarter of the 21st century, the Prime Minister emphasised that while AI can rapidly execute routine tasks to boost productivity, it must enrich rather than restrict independent thinking, allowing researchers to use saved time for harder problems, new experiments, and idea validation.“AI can give us answers quickly, but the responsibility of testing the veracity of the answer must lie with the scientist alone,” he asserted. Article Title: Act to improve last-mile broadband connectivity, COAI to govt
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: To improve last-mile connectivity in India’s broadband sector, the Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI) has urged govt to expeditiously notify the rule amendments enabling standard power operations in the delicensed lower 6 GHz band. An expert committee constituted by dept of telecom, that was led by IIT Madras’s Professor Radha Krishna Ganti had recommended enabling higher-power outdoor use at 36 dBm in the 5925–6425 MHz band. The industry has asked the telecom ministry to implement the same “without further delay”.COAI DG Lt Gen (retired) S P Kochhar said: “India's broadband sector has progressed significantly, yet last-mile connectivity gaps persist particularly in rural, semi-urban, and difficult-to-reach areas due to Right-of-Way (RoW) challenges, limited fibre availability and high deployment costs. The expert committee's recommendation to permit Standard Power (36 dBm) outdoor use of the lower 6 GHz delicensed band (5925–6425 MHz) remains a practical and cost-effective solution to this challenge — one that is yet to be operationalised through the necessary regulatory notification. ”“Fixed wireless access (FWA) and point-to-multi-point (P2MP) deployments at standard power are suited for last-mile broadband delivery where fibre penetration is absent, economically unviable or physically impractical.Enabling outdoor Standard Power operations ensures this 500 MHz of valuable delicensed spectrum is fully harnessed in service of national objectives and can be utilised by all service providers,” Kochhar said.COAI says once implemented, this move will not only expand broadband coverage but also substantially improve broadband utilisation, bringing high-quality, high-speed connectivity to homes, enterprises and institutions “that have long remained on the wrong side of the digital divide.”“Enabling these operations will ensure that India's delicensed spectrum serves not just indoor enterprise and consumer Wi-Fi but becomes a genuine engine of rural broadband penetration and digital inclusion. Several months since the Expert Committee submitted its report, COAI earnestly requests the DoT to expedite the notification of the necessary rule amendments enabling Standard Power (36 dBm) outdoor operations in the lower 6 GHz band (5925-6425 MHz) for P2MP/P2P, so as to enable licensed and authorised entities to deploy these capabilities and bring the transformative benefits of high-quality, affordable broadband to every segment of our society,” he added.
Article Summary: The Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI) has urged govt to expeditiously notify the rule amendments enabling standard power operations in the delicensed lower 6 GHz band. An expert committee constituted by dept of telecom had recommended enabling higher-power outdoor use at 36dB in the 5925–6425 MHz band.

Article Title: TOI Youth Icons Summit: CM Yogi highlights UP’s push on jobs, startups and MSMEs, says state now has 25,000 startups
Article Text:
“Earlier, districts had mafias; now, we have the One District, One Product scheme,” CM Yogi said.

Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday highlighted the state's initiatives to create employment opportunities for young people, promote startups and strengthen industries while addressing the TOI Youth Icons Summit & Awards – UP Chapter in Lucknow.Thanking The Times of India for recognising young achievers, CM Yogi said, “I would like to thank The Times of India for honouring youth icons who have done something new in their respective fields.”Referring to the changes in Uttar Pradesh over the years, the chief minister said the state had previously faced several challenges, including security concerns, mafia activity and difficulties for girls in accessing education. He contrasted this with the state's present focus on promoting products from individual districts.“Earlier, districts had mafias; now, we have the One District, One Product scheme,” he said, referring to the state's initiative to promote distinctive products from each district.“Every district has a unique product that is gaining recognition both nationally and internationally, and lakhs of young people are getting employment opportunities,” he added.Highlighting the state's micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) sector, the CM Yogi said Uttar Pradesh had 96 lakh MSME units, with the state government providing each unit with insurance cover of Rs 5 lakh.“The MSME sector in Uttar Pradesh is providing direct employment to 3.25 crore people, creating a new story of self-reliance,” he said.Speaking about government jobs, the chief minister said appointment letters had been issued for 9.5 lakh government jobs over the past nine-and-a-half years. He said recruitment had been based on merit, without special references or discrimination.“In the next six months, I will provide another one lakh government jobs to the youth of Uttar Pradesh,” he said.CM Yogi also outlined the state's plans for Agniveers after they complete four years of service under the scheme. He said the government had announced that they would have opportunities for direct recruitment in various state departments, including the police, fire services and forest department.The chief minister also highlighted employment opportunities for sportspersons, saying athletes who win medals for India would be eligible for government jobs in Uttar Pradesh.“Win a medal and get a post,” he said, referring to the policy while mentioning Prachi Chaudhary, Parul Chaudhary and Rajkumar Pal, who became deputy superintendents of police (DSPs).He added that nearly 1,400 athletes had received government job appointment letters in the state. The initiative, he said, was intended to provide athletes with a career pathway and allow them to focus on sports without worrying about their future employment.Highlighting the growth of the startup ecosystem, CM Yogi said Uttar Pradesh had moved from having 120 startups before 2017 to 25,000 currently, with lakhs of young people working in them.“The youth of Uttar Pradesh are no longer job seekers; they have become job creators,” he said, adding that the state government had established a Rs 1,000 crore fund to support startups.He also outlined plans to develop centres of excellence across the state, including a drone centre in Kanpur and a robotics centre in Noida. The government was also working towards developing centres of excellence for medical technology (MedTech) and deep technology (deep tech), he said.Under the CM Yuva Udyami Yojana, the state provides interest-free, collateral-free loans to one lakh young people every year, according to CM Yogi.“Among young people, the scheme is popularly known as CM YUVA. It is the government's own Shark Tank,” he said.The chief minister also highlighted employment opportunities in defence manufacturing, recalling a proposal he received from the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) during the 2020-21 Covid period to develop the BrahMos missile in Uttar Pradesh.He said the state offered free land in Lucknow and assured the organisation of the necessary facilities, while asking it to consider recruiting people from the state's institutions.“Eventually, 500 young engineers were selected for defence manufacturing projects through campus recruitment conducted by Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Technical University,” he said.CM Yogi added that the state was developing hyperscale data centres and global capability centres, while work was also underway to develop Lucknow as an artificial intelligence (AI) city.Speaking about women's participation in the workforce, the chief minister said the government had ensured that women could work safely during night shifts.He linked the expansion of employment opportunities for young people with the state's economic growth and improvements in connectivity.The TOI Youth Icons Summit & Awards – UP Chapter brought together achievers, emerging leaders and influential voices to celebrate young Indians shaping the country's future. The awards recognised outstanding achievers from Uttar Pradesh across categories including enterprise, sports, society, culture and social media.The summit also focused on Uttar Pradesh's transformation over the years, including developments in employment opportunities, safety and connectivity, with an emphasis on young people whose ambition, ideas and achievements are shaping India's future.
Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath addressed the TOI Youth Icons Summit & Awards – UP Chapter in Lucknow. He highlighted the state's initiatives to create employment opportunities for young people, promote startups and strengthen industries. “Earlier, districts had mafias; now, we have the One District, One Product scheme,” he said.

Article Title: New Rs 1,000 note with temple design? PIB Fact Check debunks viral claim
Article Text:
Rs 1,000 note rumour gains traction online; PIB Fact Check calls it fake

NEW DELHI: The Press Information Bureau’s (PIB) Fact Check unit on Tuesday debunked claims about a new Rs 1,000 currency note. The clarification came after images and videos of a purported yellow-coloured note featuring a temple motif went viral on social media, with some posts claiming it had been issued or would enter circulation on the 15th.PIB Fact Check clarified that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has made no announcement regarding the issuance of a new Rs 1,000 banknote.In a post on X, PIB Fact Check said, “Several social media posts claim that a new Rs 1,000 note has been issued. This claim is fake.”The agency added, “The @RBI has made no announcement regarding the issuance of a new Rs 1,000 note.” It also urged people to “Verify information through official sources and do not share unverified claims.”The clarification came after the purported note appeared in posts shared across platforms including Instagram, X and Telegram.The Rs 1,000 denomination was withdrawn from circulation during the demonetisation announced on November 8, 2016, when the government withdrew the legal tender status of the old Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes.New Rs 500 notes were subsequently introduced, while the RBI brought in Rs 2,000 notes as the highest-denomination banknotes in the new currency series.In May 2023, the RBI announced the withdrawal of Rs 2,000 notes from circulation, while clarifying that they would continue to be legal tender.Banknotes in denominations of Rs 10, Rs 20, Rs 50, Rs 100, Rs 200 and Rs 500 remain in circulation under the RBI’s Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series.PIB Fact Check has urged people to verify currency-related announcements through official sources and avoid forwarding unverified claims.The viral posts should not be treated as confirmation of a new denomination unless the RBI issues an official announcement.

The clarification came after images and videos of a purported yellow-coloured note featuring a temple motif went viral on social media. PIB Fact Check has urged people to verify currency-related announcements through official sources and avoid forwarding unverified claims.

What happens when you break the seal?

The simple open-check-store checklist

Step Action The goal 1. Check the label Look beyond the ‘Best Before’ date for instructions, such as“Refrigerate after opening and consume within 3 days.” Once opened, follow the manufacturer's guidance, as expiration dates generally apply to unopened products. Avoid handling food directly with hands or using utensils that have already been used. Reduces the risk of cross-contamination.

Quick hacks for common kitchen staples

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites
