Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Delhi liquor booking app: Buyers can now order online, 9 litres of whisky and 18 litres of beer allowed; no home delivery yet
Article Text:
(AI image) A new mobile app developed by the Delhi government's DSIIDC allows users to book liquor in advance.

Who can use the app, and what are the limits?

How the online booking facility works





NEW DELHI: Delhi residents can now book liquor bottles in advance through a mobile app developed by the Delhi State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation (DSIIDC), officials said on Tuesday.However, the facility does not include home delivery, and customers must collect their orders from the selected retail outlet within 48 hours of booking and making the online payment.The Delhi Liquor Booking app allows customers to browse available brands, select bottle sizes and quantities, and choose a DSIIDC-operated liquor store for collection. The corporation operates 208 retail outlets across the capital, and the online booking facility is currently available only at its own stores.Officials said the response to the online booking service has so far been lukewarm. Any expansion of the facility will depend on consumer response.Customers must be at least 25 years old to use the app, in accordance with the eligibility requirements. Excise rules permit an individual to purchase up to nine litres of whisky and 18 litres of beer.Once an order is booked and paid for online, the customer receives a QR code.The code can be scanned at the selected outlet to collect the liquor within 48 hours.Customers can cancel their bookings before collecting their orders. However, there is no provision for returning products once they have been sold or collected, officials said.The service is intended to reduce waiting times at liquor outlets and ease congestion at payment counters. It is also expected to improve transparency in pricing and billing while allowing customers to browse available brands before visiting a store.DSIIDC is one of four government corporations authorised to sell liquor at retail outlets in Delhi. Together, the four corporations operate more than 700 liquor vends across the capital. The online booking facility, however, is restricted to DSIIDC-operated stores.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Delhi residents can now book liquor bottles in advance through a mobile app. The app was developed by the Delhi State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation (DSIIDC) The facility does not include home delivery, and customers must collect their orders from the selected retail outlet.

Article Title: Mumbai man books Panvel flat for Rs 50 lakh in 2015, waits nearly 10 years for possession; consumer commission orders developer to refund Rs 86 lakh with 9% interest
Article Text:
AI Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





MUMBAI: Observing that a flat purchaser “cannot be expected to wait indefinitely” for possession and that the developer’s failure to hand over possession by the agreed deadline amounted to deficiency in service, a district consumer commission has directed M/s Soundlines Eco Homes and its partners to jointly and severally refund Rs 86.37 lakh (inclusive of interest) to a homebuyer over delayed possession in the “Sound Delight” project at Panvel. The commission allowed the complaint filed by Mulund resident Tapan Visaria. The pay out included the paid amount of Rs 45 lakh alongwith nine percent annual interest calculated from Dec 31, 2016, the contractual date of possession, until actual realization. He will also receive Rs 75,000 towards costs of litigation and mental agony.The commission refused to separately award Rs 5.23 lakh towards interest paid on the housing loan, relying on the Supreme Court’s decision. It was observed that the complainant had independently availed of a loan from the State Bank of India and was contractually liable to repay the loan with applicable interest. “The mere fact that the complainant incurred interest expenditure to arrange funds for purchasing the flat does not, by itself, make the opposite parties liable to reimburse that expenditure,” the Commission said while rejecting that head of claim.Visaria had booked the flat measuring 876 sq ft. carpet area, on the third floor of D-Wing in the project at Village Aashte, Taluka Panvel, District Raigad, for a total consideration of Rs 50.52 lakh. The agreement for sale was executed on Aug 7, 2015 and subsequently registered. According to the complainant, the developer had promised possession on or before Dec 31, 2016, but repeatedly extended the timeline, with the MahaRERA website later reflecting an extension up to Sept 30, 2026.The complainant alleged that he paid around Rs 45.45 lakh towards the flat consideration, apart from Rs 1.38 lakh towards VAT, GST and other taxes, Rs 2.53 lakh towards stamp duty and Rs 30,000 towards registration charges. He also claimed that amenities advertised in the project brochure, including an entrance gate with waterfall, clubhouse, rooftop shamiyana, amphitheatre and children’s play area, were either cancelled or not provided as promised.The opposite parties, including the partnership firm and its partners did not appear despite service of notices. The matter was therefore proceeded ex parte by order dated April 16, 2024. Taking note of the unrebutted material placed by the complainant, the commission said the agreement, bank statements, demand letters, email correspondence, photographs and loan interest certificate established that the flat had been booked and substantial payment had been made. “The evidence on record establishes that the opposite parties failed to deliver possession within the agreed period and have not furnished any satisfactory explanation for the delay. Such failure amounts to deficiency in service,” the commission held.
Article Summary: A district consumer commission has directed M/s Soundlines Eco Homes and its partners to jointly and severally refund Rs 86.37 lakh. The commission allowed the complaint filed by Mulund resident Tapan Visaria. The pay out included the paid amount of Rs 45 lakh alongwith nine percent annual interest calculated from Dec 31, 2016, the contractual date of possession.

Article Title: We’ve reduced mafia to dust in UP, says CM Yogi Adityanath
Article Text:
Yogi Adityanath spoke at the Youth Icon Awards, emphasizing the changes in Uttar Pradesh since 2017.





LUCKNOW: “Humnein mafia ko mitti mein mila diya hai,” said chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday, describing the impact of his govt’s zero tolerance policy towards crime since 2017 that had resulted in better facilities, economic growth and investments in the state.Speaking at the TOI Youth Icon Awards, UP Chapter, organised by The Times of India in Lucknow, the CM said that criminals were now grovelling for leniency, saying that they would happily sell bananas but move away from crime.After the implementation of BJP ’s zero tolerance policy towards crime from 2017, UP was no longer identified with ‘one district-one mafia’, he said.Describing the positive changes in UP since 2017, the CM also appealed to the youth to not allow forces, which had forced the previous generation into depression and disappointment, to return to power, using their power of the vote to ensure that the right people were elected.“There was a time when it was difficult for girls to even go to school. In many west UP districts, families were forced to send their daughters to other states to study. Now, girls work without any fear till even 2 am because there is an atmosphere of security,” Yogi said.The CM honoured 37 youth icons from various fields, like sports, entrepreneurship, art, culture, social work and digital creation. He commended TOI for felicitating youth, as this would then inspire lakhs of others to follow their dreams.Among the awardees were 10 sportspersons from UP, including Parul Chaudhary, Raj Kumar Pal and Arjun Deshwal. Gorakhpur MP Ravi Kishan was recognised as the Youth Icon of the Year, while Himanshu Bajpai won for promoting regional language.The female entrepreneur of the year award went to fashion designer Mili Malhotra while Mayank, the founder of multinational IT firm Adrosonic, was adjudged the male entrepreneur of the year.Yashoda, aka English Dehati, was awarded for Digital Education and Language Learning, Shinjini Kulkarni for Performing Arts and Maroof Culmen for Food and Culture. Abhishek Pandey, district magistrate of Pratapgarh, was recognised for Social Impact.The CM described eight major changes that have happened in UP since 2017, citing how these helped change the state’s image, pushing it from the bottom three economies to the top three. Not only had the state’s economy grown by three times but also per capita income and the state’s budget.He said that UP’s youth had moved away from being job seekers to becoming job givers. “Better security, availability of continuous power supply, sectoral policies, AI and technology and improved infrastructure have improved confidence and brought investment in the state,” he said.“In 2047, by when India will be Viksit Bharat as promised by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the youth and those honoured at this event, will be around 40-45 years old. They will be leading the country. Therefore, they must prepare for the future from now on through their talent and hard work,” the CM said.“In a democracy, voting is not just your right but also your duty. You should vote wisely to ensure that the disappointments that pushed the previous generation into disappointment do not return. Those who spread anarchy, created an unsafe environment, allowed potholes, should not be allowed to return,” he said.The CM also highlighted the importance of India’s democracy, saying that had there been no democracy, it would not have been possible for comedians to crack jokes on stage, for people to make speeches since everything would have been censored. “Freedom of speech within ‘maryada’ is guaranteed for everyone,” he said.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath spoke at the TOI Youth Icon Awards, UP Chapter, organised by The Times of India in Lucknow. He said that criminals were now grovelling for leniency, saying that they would happily sell bananas but move away from crime.

Article Title: Delhi Police busts cyber fraud gang over Rs 3.9 crore scam involving 149 transactions; 7 arrested in money laundering and USDT cryptocurrency racket
Article Text:
Delhi police arrests 7 in major cyber fraud case (Representative image)





NEW DELHI: Delhi Police’s Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit has busted a cyber fraud network after a businessman lost Rs 3.9 crore in 149 unauthorised transactions. The racket allegedly laundered the money through mule accounts, cash withdrawals and hawala channels before using a foreign exchange application to convert it into USDT cryptocurrency. Seven people have been arrested.The case was reported by Prince Bansal (28), who deals in non-banking financial company (NBFC) and loan-related transactions. He told police that Rs 3.9 crore was debited from his bank account without his knowledge on Oct 5. The National Cybercrime Reporting Portal has since placed a lien on Rs 1.7 crore of the stolen funds.DCP (IFSO) Gaurav Tyagi stated that a seven-day investigation across Rajasthan led to the arrest of a cyber fraud suspect Brij Lal (29) in Phalodi. Lal, who was tracked through bank transactions, was also wanted in a separate Rs 95 lakh cyber fraud case.Investigators revealed that the fraudsters routed the funds through multiple bank accounts before withdrawing cash.Some accused allegedly arranged accounts in their names or facilitated the use of accounts belonging to others. Police arrested co-accused Piyush Talaniya (19), who allegedly sent Rs 9.5 lakh to Lal, and Vipin Chanwariya (19), who allegedly withdrew Rs 7 lakh on Lal’s instructions on Oct 12.During questioning, Lal disclosed that he had a wallet ID on the money-exchange application and used cash to buy USDT via a hawala operator, some of which was delivered to a contact in Khanna.Police recovered 45 cheque books, 45 ATM cards, 25 passbooks and 13 mobile phones. Further investigation is under way to establish the money trail and identify remaining network members.
Article Summary: The case was reported by Prince Bansal (28), who deals in non-banking financial company (NBFC) transactions. He told police that Rs 3.9 crore was debited from his bank account without his knowledge on Oct 5. The National Cybercrime Reporting Portal has since placed a lien on Rs 1.7 crore of the stolen funds.

Article Title: SIR final list for Karnataka is out: Check your name, download electoral roll PDF and find updated serial number
Article Text:
Karnataka has completed the Special Intensive Revision of the electoral roll after 129 days of processing (File photo)





BENGALURU: After a 129-day exercise, the final electoral roll under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has been published. Voters may look up their part number and serial number on the ECI website by entering the district, constituency and part number.The rolls are downloadable in PDF format. Voters can also look up their details using the serial number on their voter ID card.Voters may check their status using this link: https://voters.eci.gov.in/download-eroll?stateCode=S10 During the publication of the draft rolls on August 24, several voters' part and serial numbers were updated. However one would find updated details on the ECINet app using your EPIC number .SIR in Karnataka began with the verification of the state's 5.5 crore voters (5,54,32,314) on the electoral roll (as on June 16).In the first round of deletions, reflected in the draft roll published on August 24, the state lost about 20% of its voters to the ASDDO (Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate and Others) classification.The largest chunk of voters removed from the draft list were those classified as 'permanently shifted'. This category accounted for 65.45 lakh voters, or 11.8% of the ASDDO list.The two-month claims, notices and objections phase, which began on August 24, saw about 43.8 lakh of the 4.4 crore draft listed voters (4,46,35,975) being issued notices.Officials said that about 60,000 of them were excluded from the final list. Claims and objections could be filed only during the first month of this phase, until September 23.Between June 16 and September 23, 7.87 lakh citizens sought inclusion in the final voter list through Form 6 applications, while 4,530 NRIs sought inclusion through Form 6A.Objections to existing voters and requests for deletion, filed either by voters themselves or their families, amounted to 58,475. Meanwhile, 10.99 lakh voters from the draft list sought modifications to their details, ranging from spelling corrections to changes in polling booth locations.The SIR activity in the state began on June 20, with the deployment of 59,050 booth-level officers (BLOs), 332 Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) and 224 Electoral Registration Officers (EROs).There were 5,905 BLO supervisors, each overseeing 10 BLOs. The district commissioners were designated as District Election Officers (DEOs), with 34 such officers across the state.The number of BLOs and AEROs increased over time to 60,932 and 4,258, respectively.Recognised political parties appointed 1.33 lakh booth-level agents (BLAs) during the enumeration phase to ensure the forms reached voters.These BLAs were also instrumental in filing objections against voters on the list during the subsequent claims and objections period.The enumeration phase began on June 30 and was granted two extensions. While it was originally scheduled to end on July 29, the CEO's office announced a 10-day extension to August 8 on July 15, owing to the large number of voters requiring ASDDO classification.The deadline was subsequently extended by another 10 days.
Article Summary: The rolls are downloadable in PDF format. Voters can also look up their details using the serial number on their voter ID card. The SIR activity in the state began on June 20, with the deployment of 59,050 booth-level officers (BLOs) and 224 Electoral Registration Officers (EROs)

Article Title: Red alert for 11 Andhra districts: Schools shut, over 50 trains cancelled as Cyclone Arnab nears landfall; storm threatens flights to Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada
Article Text:
The IMD has issued rainfall warnings of varying severity for coastal Andhra Pradesh and adjoining areas, with the highest level of alert covering several districts on Tuesday and Wednesday.





VISAKHAPATNAM: As severe Cyclone Arnab is expected to make landfall between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, on Wednesday, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 115–125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph, the Andhra Pradesh government has stepped up precautionary measures.Educational institutions in coastal districts have been closed, sea fishing operations prohibited and rescue teams kept on standby at various locations to ensure zero loss of life and minimal damage to infrastructure.The rainfall activity with strong gales began in parts of Kakinada, Konaseema, Anakapalle, Visakhapatnam, and a few other districts on Tuesday morning. The locals in Vizag city the sea conditions turned rough on Tuesday morning.The rainfall activity may intensify from Tuesday afternoon.The very severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” over Westcentral Bay of Bengal moved nearly westwards with a speed of 22 kmph during past six hours, and lay centered 260 km southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 300 km east-southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 380 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha), 390 km east of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 460 km east of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh) and 980 km west-northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands).It is very likely to move west-northwestwards till Tuesday (Oct 27) evening. Thereafter, it is very likely to move northwestwards and cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on Wednesday October (28) afternoon. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on October 27 and 28.The IMD has issued rainfall warnings of varying severity for coastal Andhra Pradesh and adjoining areas, with the highest level of alert covering several districts on Tuesday and Wednesday.For Tuesday, a red warning for extremely heavy rainfall has been issued for Anakapalle, Kakinada, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari and Eluru districts, as well as Yanam.An orange warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall is in force for Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Visakhapatnam, NTR, Krishna, Guntur and Bapatla districts. A yellow warning for heavy rainfall has been issued for Palnadu, Prakasam and Nellore districts.For Wednesday, red warnings have been issued for Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalle, Kakinada, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, NTR, Krishna and Guntur districts.Orange warnings cover Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram and Bapatla districts, as well as Yanam, while yellow warnings have been issued for Palnadu, Prakasam and Nellore districts.In view of the imminent cyclone Arnab and in the interest of passenger safety, south coastal railway cancelled more than 50 trains running between Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Kakinada, and few other destinations on Tuesday and Wednesday.Passengers have been advised to check train-wise cancellation details, confirm their journey dates and verify train status before heading to stations.The weather conditions associated with cyclone Arnab may impact flights to and from Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada.However, as of now there are no cancellation of flights from ASR international airport, Bhogapuram and all operations are normal on Tuesday.
Article Summary: Cyclone Arnab is expected to make landfall between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, on Wednesday. The Andhra Pradesh government has stepped up precautionary measures. The rainfall activity with strong gales began in parts of Kakinada, Konaseema, Anakapalle, and a few other districts on Tuesday morning.

Article Title: Plan to cut 400+ trees for 2nd GMLR flyover & interchange
Article Text:
This proposal impacts more than 400 trees, including 187 mangroves, and falls within ecologically sensitive areas (Representative image)

NOC for marina sought

New GAIL pipeline

Aid for Ratnagiri beach





MUMBAI: Over 400 trees, including 187 mangroves, could be affected as regulator Maharashtra Coastal Zone Management Authority (MCZMA) has recommended to the Union environment ministry BMC’s proposal for a second flyover as part of the Goregaon-Mulund Link Road corridor (phase 4) and a clover leaf interchange with four left passes.The clover leaf interchange is proposed through an ecologically sensitive zone (CRZ IA), a mangrove and mangrove buffer zone (CRZ IA), an intertidal zone (CRZ IB) and CRZ II.Some part of the flyover falls in CRZ IA as also the free lefts from Thane to Airoli, Thane to Nahur, and Airoli to Mumbai. Compensatory afforestation has been proposed in Chandrapur district, for which over 4 hectares will be provided in Amdi Begde village.MCZMA has submitted an application to the Thane creek flamingo sanctuary as the project will fall within its eco-sensitive zone.MCZMA also directed the project proponent of the proposed inland water transport terminal (marina) at Cuffe Parade to obtain an NOC from MMRDA stating that it is not in conflict with the Nariman Point-Colaba/Cuffe Parade bridge.The bridge is currently under the Union environment ministry’s consideration.The total built-up area for the project has been scaled down from 35,000sqm to 18,600sqm.The project components include foreshore facilities such as promenade, an immigration centre on 10,000sqm of reclaimed land, a jetty, a road, a ramp for yachts and a breakwater navigational channel, a turning circle and a floatel.For the MMRDA bridge, MCZMA has introduced a fresh clause—10.3—replacing the earlier 5.3(c) of CRZ norms to explain the structure’s permissibility.Clause 10.3 specifically applies to Mumbai city and suburbs and designates all open spaces as non-development zones.MCZMA also recommended to the Union ministry a proposal by GAIL to augment the Dahej-Uran-Dabhol-Panvel natural gas pipeline’s capacity to meet growing demand in Raigad and Ratnagiri districts.The Centre has been pushing for augmentation of LNG services since the start of the Iran-US war.The proposed 105km pipeline will run parallel to the existing corridor. No mangrove cutting is involved in its laying.The regulator approved financial assistance of Rs 1.5 lakh per month for a year for Ladghar beach in Ratnagiri district, which has been selected for the Centre’s blue flag certification scheme.In all, five beaches in Maharashtra have been selected for the scheme, of which Ladghar, Shrivardhan and Guhaghar are likely to be recommended to the national jury.The local gram panchayat had sent a letter stating it does not have sufficient financial resources to pay the beach manager, two security guards and four housekeeping staff.The objective of the blue flag programme is to conserve and maintain the beach environment with sustainable development.
Article Summary: Over 400 trees, including 187 mangroves, could be affected by a proposal for a second flyover. Compensatory afforestation has been proposed in Chandrapur district. The regulator approved financial assistance of Rs 1.5 lakh per month for a year for Ladghar beach in Ratnagiri district.

Article Summary: Tata Sons vs Tata Trusts: Both sides explore insurance cover as legal battle looms. Both sides are seeking to avoid a potential court battle over Tata Sons' control of the Tata Trust. Tata Sons is the holding company of Tata Group, which includes Tata Group Trusts.
